nodes.name: IF pretreatment
nodes.procedure: The commercial IF (1.0 cm × 2.0 cm) was pickled and washed with 0.1 mol L⁻¹ HCl, acetone, and ethanol for 20 min each and subsequently dried in a vacuum to remove impurities from the surface.
nodes.source_text: the commercial IF (1.0 cm × 2.0 cm) was pickled and washed with 0.1 mol L⁻¹ HCl, acetone, and ethanol for 20 min each and subsequently dried in a vacuum

nodes.name: RuNi-Fe2O3/IF hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: The washed IFs were placed in a clear and transparent aqueous solution composed of same mole ratio of NiCl₂·6H₂O, RuCl₃·3H₂O and 50 mL DI water, transferred to a 100 mL Teflon-lined stainless autoclave, heated from room temperature to 150 °C for 6 h, and then naturally cooled to room temperature. The sample was removed, washed several times with DI water and ethanol, and dried under vacuum at 60 °C.

nodes.name: Pt/C electrode preparation
nodes.procedure: 5 mg Pt/C was homogeneously dispersed with the aid of 30 min of ultrasonication in a solution containing 500 μL deionized water, 495 μL ethanol, and 5 μL Nafion mixed solution to form an ink. After dipping, the uniform ink mixture was dropped onto clean IF (1.0 cm × 2.0 cm) and then dried in an oven.

nodes.characterization_summary: Lattice fringe spacings of 0.25 nm and 0.30 nm ascribed to the (311) and (220) crystal planes of Fe2O3.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HRTEM image in Fig. 1(d) reveals that the apparent lattice fringe spacing of 0.25 and 0.30 nm are ascribed to the (311) and (220) crystal planes of Fe2O3, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Uniform distribution of Ru, Ni, Fe, and O throughout the lily structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ru/Ni doping can be evidenced by the TEM element mapping result (Fig. 1(j)), which displays a uniform distribution of Ru and Ni throughout the lily in addition to Fe and O.

nodes.characterization_summary: Sharp diffraction peaks at 44.6° and 65.1° for Fe(110) and (200) planes; peaks at 30.2°, 35.6°, 43.3°, 53.7°, 57.3°, and 62.9° for Fe2O3 (220), (311), (400), (422), (511), and (440) planes; no extra phases detected.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 2(a), the sharp diffraction peaks at 44.6° and 65.1° can be ascribed to the (110) and (200) planes of the Fe substrate... other peaks centered at 30.2°, 35.6°, 43.3°, 53.7°, 57.3°, and 62.9° corresponding to the (220), (311), (400), (422), (511), and (440) planes of Fe2O3.

nodes.characterization_summary: RuNi-Fe2O3/IF survey shows Ru, Ni, Fe, O present; Fe 2p: 710.1/724.2 eV (Fe2+), 712.2/727.4 eV (Fe3+); Ni 2p: 872.7/855.2 eV (Ni2+) with satellites 878.9/860.9 eV; Ru 3p: 484.8/461.3 eV; positive shifts in Fe and Ni binding energies after dual doping indicate electronic interactions between dopants and Fe2O3 host.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As seen from the XPS survey spectra, Ru, Ni, Fe, and O are notably detected in RuNi-Fe2O3/IF... The Fe 2p spectrum in Fig. 2(b) reveals that the two peaks at 710.1 and 724.2 eV can be attributed to Fe2+ 2p3/2 and Fe2+ 2p1/2... Compared with those of the Ni-Fe2O3/IF and Ru-Fe2O3/IF control samples, the binding energy of Fe displays a positive shift after Ni or Ru doping.
